title: Grill — Harness account stacks (round 2: push-back + remaining shape)

credentials-recheck.title: Copying the primary's credential files makes the backup the same provider account. Do you still want that?
credentials-recheck.display: Each member uses its own login

mirror-scope.title: "Mirror everything" includes hooks and permissions, which execute code. What exactly should be mirrored?
mirror-scope.note: when I say tokens, I mean the authenticated oauth for mcp, plugins,etc. but the harness login/account should be separated, so it works correcly each account with its own limits

v1-kinds-recheck.title: You chose Claude + Codex only, but the acceptance default you confirmed mentions an OpenCode adapter. Which is the v1 scope?

after-swap.title: After a swap, where does the task run next?
after-swap.note: it must return to the primary only if the last stack account reaches the limit, then a natural swap to the beginning of the stack happens, ie. going to the primary. We just need to make sure that if all accounts are tried in a run, to avoid running the train in loop, we must pause, as a cap.

home-tools.title: Codex aliases override HOME, so the backup loses `~/.gitconfig`, `~/.ssh`, `~/.config/gh` and `~/.npmrc`. What should v1 do?
home-tools.display: Build a HOME overlay for the five kinds

swap-notice.title: What should the in-transcript swap message look like?
swap-notice.display: A status divider with structured text

orphans.title: What happens to pending permission/question cards, running background agents, and queued follow-ups when the account swaps?
orphans.display: Cancel cards, keep follow-ups, name abandoned agents

lifecycle.title: When a stack is created or a member is disabled, deleted, reordered or removed, when do tasks pick up the change?

manual-switch.title: When the user manually switches a task to another member of the same stack, should the conversation be preserved?
manual-switch.display: Preserve within the stack, reset outside

synthetic-prompt.title: Should the synthetic "continue" prompt be visible in the transcript?
synthetic-prompt.display: Hidden from the transcript, tagged in storage

proactive-reactive.title: How is the next member chosen?
proactive-reactive.value: Both: skip a member whose cached quota clearly says exhausted, and react to a failure as the backstop. A stale or missing snapshot never blocks a run on its own.

exhaustion-scope.title: Is exhaustion account-global or per task?
exhaustion-scope.value: Account-global: a new `harness_limit_state` table (no FK, like `harness_usage`) with `exhausted_until_ms`, reason, source and message. Selection skips a cooling account in every task; it clears on a successful turn or on expiry. No concurrency reservation in v1.

max-size-followup.title: What follows from "no maximum" stack size?
max-size-followup.value: No hard cap. The stack editor virtualizes long lists and shows a warning above 10 members; the swap UI shows position/count; selection stays O(n) per turn.

rollout.title: What is the rollout gate?
rollout.value: No global feature flag. Stacks are opt-in by creating one, so an existing user sees no behavior change until they build a stack.

per-task-opt-out.title: Can a single task opt out of failover?
per-task-opt-out.value: No per-task opt-out in v1. A task that must stay on one account uses an account that is not in a stack.
